title: Concrete Pump Reducer / Taper Pipe: Where Plugs Start
seoTitle: Concrete Pump Reducer and Taper Pipe | Pinjin Xingtai
description: ACPA: reducers and bends create turbulence; a reducer is usually the first place to look when a plug occurs. Pinjin does not list a reducer SKU or a factory taper table. Quote delivery pipe after the pump DN — Electric 20 is 80 mm; Electric 15 is 100–125 mm.

answerBlock.what: ACPA’s study guide: reducers and bends in the placing line create turbulence. A lean or poorly graded mix may not pass; a reducer is usually the first place to look when a plug occurs. If the reducer rises under pressure but the hose is soft, the plug is in the reducer. Pinjin does not list a reducer or taper-pipe SKU and does not publish a factory reducer table. We quote [delivery pipe](/products/concrete-pump-delivery-pipe/) after the pump model and DN. Electric 20 lists 80 mm; Electric 15 lists 100–125 mm. Do not invent a transition that is not written on those pages.
answerBlock.who: Buyers assembling a pipeline who saw “reducer” on a marketplace hose kit and need to match a listed Pinjin DN, not a competitor taper chart.
factors: Start from the DN printed on the pump page
ACPA: inspect the reducer first when a plug forms; never open a coupling under pressure
Pinjin has no published reducer SKU or wall-thickness taper table
Quote straight pipe, clamps and hose after model, DN and quantity

faqs.question: Does Pinjin sell a catalogue concrete pump reducer?
faqs.answer: No reducer or taper-pipe SKU is listed on the parts hub. We quote straight delivery pipe, DN80 clamps, hoses and the DN200 90° elbow after size and quantity. A marketplace ‘reducer’ listing is not a Pinjin table. Send the pump model and both diameters if you still need a transition quoted from Xingtai — unpublished dimensions are not promised here.

faqs.question: Can I drop Electric 15’s 100–125 mm line onto Electric 20’s 80 mm pipe with any taper?
faqs.answer: We do not publish that transition. Electric 20 lists 80 mm pipe. Electric 15 lists 100–125 mm. The older DN article says clamps and hoses continue the pump diameter unless engineers agree a documented transition — and that page does not print a reducer table. Do not splice two model rows.

faqs.question: Where should I look first if the line plugs after a diameter change?
faqs.answer: ACPA: a reducer is usually the first place to look. If the reducer rises as pressure is applied and the hose stays soft, the plug is in the reducer. Relieve pressure before opening any coupling. See the blockage safety page. Do not use compressed air to force a plug.
